subject: Latency & Throughput agreement — Dedicated GPU pilot checklist
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Anna Gomez <anna@olivetech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot recap — latency/throughput targets and dedicated sizing proposal

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so we have the same expectations for the Dedicated pilot.

Summary of customer constraints (from call)
- Target p95 latency: ~300ms for typical responses (~200–300 tokens)
- Baseline throughput: 60 req/s sustained, with expected bursts up to 200 concurrent active requests
- Streaming required: token-by-token streaming to the client (low tail latency important)
- Region preference: us-west-2 (data residency + proximity)

Preliminary Dedicated plan (what we propose for the pilot)
- GPUs to bench: H100 80GB (high-concurrency config) and A100 80GB (cost baseline)
- Reserved throughput: start with 80 rps reserved, burst pool to 200 (policy: autoscale + capped burst credit)
- Concurrency model: 8–12 concurrent streams per GPU (depends on sequence length & quantization)
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts (we’ll instrument cache hit metrics)
- Acceptance criteria (pilot pass): p95 <= 350ms at 60 rps sustained for 256-token responses, and graceful degradation to 200 rps with 95% availability

Action items we’ll take next (attached / linked)
1) Redwood: run bench with both H100 and A100 on customer-supplied prompt set (we need the sample prompts) — target 48-hour benchmark window. (Attachment: pilot-config-proposal.xlsx)
2) OliveTech: provide a 50–100 representative prompt set + 3 typical request payloads and a representative session streaming pattern. (Attachment: sample-prompts.txt)
3) Agree on pilot timeline and sign the pilot MSA addendum (I attached a draft SLA we can iterate on).

Can you confirm the prompts and whether SOC2 evidence is required before the pilot (we can pull the SOC2 report but will need an NDA if you want more detailed logs)? Also confirm the billing/PO contact so we can reserve capacity.

Proposed next touchpoints
- Bench kickoff: Wed 6/28 (we’ll need prompts by EOD Tue 6/27)
- Mid-pilot sync: 72 hours after bench starts
- Pilot close: ~10 business days after bench completion

Attached: pilot-config-proposal.xlsx, sample-prompts.txt

Thanks — I’ll loop in Karthik/Ben on the bench plan after your confirmation.

—
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Anna Gomez <anna@olivetech.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot recap — latency/throughput targets and dedicated sizing proposal

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the priorities from our side and a few clarifications:

Confirmed priorities
- p95 latency is the target we care most about; 300ms is ideal, 350ms is acceptable as a stretch for the pilot.
- Sustained throughput of 60 req/s is accurate; bursts to 200 are realistic during campaign spikes.
- Streaming is required (we stream partial replies into our UI as tokens arrive).

Clarifications / asks
- Can you quantify what "8–12 concurrent streams per GPU" means for 256-token median responses? We have a mix of short (50–80 tokens) and long (250–400 tokens) responses — the long ones drive tail latency.
- Region must be us-west-2. Can the bench run there?
- We will need SOC2 TYPE II evidence and a short security questionnaire answered before we put internal PII into the pilot data. I can send the questionnaire today.
- Cost: we need a rough order of magnitude for a 2-week pilot (GPU-hours + reserved throughput). A ballpark estimate is fine to start procurement.

We’ll attach a 75-sample prompt set and the questionnaire by EOD today. Please confirm the kickoff on 6/28 if Redwood can run bench in us-west-2.

Anna
Anna Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering, OliveTech
anna@olivetech.com | +1 206-555-0114

Karthik / Ben —

OliveTech confirmed the constraints — p95 target ~300–350ms for mixed token lengths, sustained 60 rps with bursts to 200, region must be us-west-2. They will send a 75-sample prompt set and a security questionnaire today.

Ask: can you propose a bench configuration for us-west-2 that compares H100 80GB vs A100 80GB and includes:
- reserved throughput target (start 80 rps with burst bucket to 200)
- concurrency mapping (expected streams per GPU for short / long responses)
- a lightweight quantization test (FP16 vs 4-bit) and observable regression thresholds (quality delta < 1.5% on our eval set)

Timeline: bench kickoff 6/28 MDT — I need a runnable bench script and estimated GPU-hours today so I can confirm with OliveTech procurement. Also flag any obvious blockers (SOC2 docs we need to share).

Thanks — Maya

Anna —

Thanks for sending the prompt set and the questionnaire overnight. High-level update and confirmed next steps after internal sizing: we can run the bench in us-west-2 and propose an H100-first pilot with an A100 run for cost comparison.

What we’ll run (48-hour bench window)
- H100 80GB profile: optimistic latency mode (higher concurrency, aggressive kernel selection)
- A100 80GB profile: conservative mode (lower concurrency, cost baseline)
- Quantization vector: FP16 baseline -> 4-bit int8-like profile; will record quality delta on your eval subset
- Workload: your 75 prompts with streaming client pattern (token sizes reflect mix you provided)

Reserved throughput proposal
- Start reserved: 80 rps (gives headroom above the 60 rps baseline)
- Burst capacity: pooled credit to 200 rps with autoscale policy and fallback to A100 variant if H100 capacity is constrained
- Acceptance: p95 <= 350ms at 60 rps sustained for 256-token responses; pass if quality delta <= 1.5% on eval set and system retains >95% availability under burst testing

Estimated resource ask (ballpark)
- Bench GPU-hours: H100 80GB -> 40 GPU-hours; A100 80GB -> 32 GPU-hours (we’ll provide an exact number post-sanity run)
- Pilot reserved window (2 weeks): estimate ~240 GPU-hours (we’ll provide pricing tiers; this is an estimate for procurement)

Attachments: updated pilot-sla-draft.pdf (low-friction SLA and pilot MSA addendum), and a Drive link with bench scripts: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/olivetech/pilot-bench-2028

Next steps for OliveTech
1) Sign the pilot addendum (I’ll send DocuSign after you confirm).
2) Confirm PO/billing contact and whether we can share SOC2 Type II (we can share sanitized artifacts).
3) Final confirmation on kickoff (we propose Mon 7/1 09:00 PT so we have a full week for bench + 1 week pilot).

If that schedule looks ok I’ll kick off the H100 bench on Mon 7/1.

Best —
Maya Srinivasan
